newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds open slightly weaker in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds open slightly weaker in quiet trade.

text.p: Canadian bonds recovered from an overnight selling bias to open slightly weaker in quiet trading on Tuesday after the release of economic data indicating moderate inflationary pressures in the U.S. economy, dealers said.

The U.S. Department of Commerce reported June retail sales rose 0.5 percent compared to a downwardly revised 0.3 percent decline in May. When excluding the key automobile component, retail sales rose 0.3 percent.
A Reuters survey had forecast a 0.2 percent rise in sales and a 0.5 percent increase minus the automobile component.

"The marginally weaker-than-expected retail sales numbers are giving Canadian bonds the room to come back from last night's selling," said Harvinder Kalirai, Canadian analyst with New York-based I.D.E.A.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$0.19 to C$118.30 to yield 6.590 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond fell 3/32 to yield 6.56 percent. The spread between the bonds remained three basis points, the same as at the close of trading on Friday.
Analysts said the direction of bonds would depend on U.S. and Canadian economic data due to be released later this week.
"If tomorrow's CPI number in the U.S. holds up pretty well, then bonds could move higher," Kalirai said.
Canadian economic reports out this week include the consumer price index for June out on Thursday, and merchandise and wholesale trade data for May out Friday.
Analysts U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony on July 22 would be the next large hurdle for the Canadian bond market.
"We're stuck in a range until the Humphrey-Hawkins testimony next week," said Rob Palombi, senior fixed-income analyst with MMS International.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond fell C$0.11 to C$109.00 to yield 6.025 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond fell 2/32 to yield 6.26 percent.
The negative spread between the two benchmark bonds was 24 basis points, unchanged from Monday's close.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 3.18 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 5.21 percent.
